description: Upper port of terminal-control, addressed by key. Callers (the Node client behind the internal route, /fgOS:terminal) see only these operations; the multiplexer lives behind a driver (driver-capabilities.v1.json). terminal-control knows nothing about runs, deadlines, receipts or work items.

key.meaning: caller-chosen id of one slot: today the round's launchCommandId or ad-hoc round id, later the attempt id. One key names at most one pane for its whole life.

groupKey.meaning: panes of one group share a tab: unit run id, or workflow run id when there is one. Display only for herdr; never a lock.

fields.label: string; tab label for the group and pane label for the slot

display.rule: display is written to the terminal and the record only; no code reads it back to decide anything

input.roleHint: optional string; structured data for the placement policy only
input.cwd: optional absolute path: working directory of the new pane's shell
input.env: optional object of string: environment of the new pane's shell

effects: places a new pane through the placement policy (placement-policy.v1.json) when the driver has layout.geometry, otherwise splits the newest live group pane down at 0.3 and applies maxPanesPerTab by pane count
a group with no live pane gets a new tab whose first pane is the slot itself (no empty root pane)
publishes the allocation record (allocation-record.v1.json) once, with link(2)
an allocate for a key that already has a record returns that record's slot when the pane is live, unknown otherwise; it never allocates a second pane for one key

input.groupKey: optional groupKey: the pane joins that group so its next pane opens beside it; defaults to the key

effects: records origin attached; core never closes an attached pane, release only removes its label and link

launchSpec.activity: optional {kind, args, timeoutMs}: start through the driver's agent support (activity.state) instead of a plain pane.run; timeoutMs bounds how long the driver may take to bring the agent to ready
launchSpec.expect: optional {argv0, command, args}: the foreground process the launch becomes when it is not the command itself (a launcher script that execs the real one); identity is taken from the process matching it

effects: requires pane.run, read.screen and process.info for plain launch; activity.state and process.info for activity launch
plain launch types probe commands to prove shell execution before the marker is written
writes marker launch-requested after the ready-shell handshake succeeds, before typing the launch line
writes marker launched{identity} after the root process of the pane command is identified (argv checked like verifyForegroundProcessArgv)
returns not-started if launch was already requested, if pane foreground is not the shell, if pane shell did not become ready in time, or if the launched root process was not identified in time
never launches into a slot that already has launch-requested

send.rule: exactly one of text or keys; nothing is typed unless a process other than the pane's shell (or the launched command that exec-replaced it) holds the foreground, also through the prompt door (submit)

input.detail: optional boolean: add the driver's detector verdict to activity.detail
input.foreground: optional boolean, default true: false skips reading the foreground process
input.activity: optional boolean, default true: false skips reading the agent state

input.until: retain only: epoch ms, or null for kept until a person closes it
input.callerPane: optional driver pane id: the pane the caller itself runs in; only a close of an attached slot whose pane equals it closes the pane

effects: close: closes only the pane this key allocated, only when the server incarnation matches right before and right after the close; never closes a tab
retain: records released{retain, until}; a later reconcile closes only past until, same incarnation, foreground not foreign

attached slots: release removes label and link only, except a close whose callerPane is the slot's own pane (a person closing their own pane through /fgOS:terminal-close), which closes it like an allocated pane (same incarnation checks); the only exception

input.reportState: optional string: also tell the driver which agent (display.agent) runs in the pane, for a process it does not recognise on its own; the reported state becomes the pane's status authority

capabilities.meaning: driver name, declared capability list (driver-capabilities.v1.json) and current server incarnation or unknown; doctor reads this

reconcile-scan.rule: reports only; never closes anything because time passed (except retain past until under the release rule)

foreground-not-agent.reason: string; nothing was typed: the pane's shell is in the foreground, or its foreground could not be read or identified

inspection.foreground: optional identity of the foreground process
inspection.activity: optional {state, agent, session, detail}; present only when the driver declares activity.state; detail = {state, visibleBlocker, visibleIdle, visibleWorking, matchedRule, promptText} only when asked for

kept-unknown.reason: string; the pane is kept because the core could not prove it may close it

findings.paneId: string | null; the pane the finding is about, null when no record names one

unsupported.capability: the missing capability name, or driver-absent

unknown.reason: string; driver timeout, unreadable output, incarnation mismatch, or missing record

identity.startTime: string (clock ticks since boot on Linux)

invariants: every operation has explicit unsupported and unknown results; the core never guesses
unknown is never turned into gone or closed
the core closes only panes it allocated, by key, and never closes a tab
labels are display only; no code reads a label to decide
a pane taken with attach is never closed by the core, except on a close that names that pane as the caller's own (callerPane)
